slope_threshold_source: Forbidden = suit.json max_slope_deg (15 deg, Martian Map assumption, see its source). Caution at 10 deg: team proposal
V_source: ICES-2026-127 slide 9: 2.2 mph, maximum nominal Apollo walking speed
L_source: 104 kg suit (229 lbm max Mars suit) + 22.7 kg tools/samples (50 lbm), ICES-2026-127
eta_source: Soule & Goldman 1972: dirt road 1.1, loose sand 2.1. Mapping from roughness to eta and rough_ref = 0.5 m are our assumption
gRatio_source: Mars gravity = 3/8 g, scaling Pandolf by 0.38 is our assumption
cell_m_source: mock grid cell size, the real value comes from meta.json
P_nom_source: ICES-2026-127: 1200 BTU/hr x 0.29307 W per BTU/hr
tobler_source: Tobler 1993 hiking function (km/h). Designed for unsuited hikers, we use it only to slow down on steep slopes. Our assumption for suited Mars EVA
gcr_mSv_per_h_source: Hassler et al. 2014, Science 343: MSL/RAD average GCR dose equivalent of 0.67 mSv/day at Gale Crater (sols 1-300), divided by 24 h
gcr_assumption: RAD's 0.67 mSv/day is as per Earth day (24 h).
gcr_uncertainty_source: Hassler et al. 2014 as cited in SWSC 2016 reports 0.67 +/- 0.12 mSv/day, applied here to the 0.67 mSv/day rate as an approximation (our assumption)

depot_per_tube.source: Apollo 16: ~3 min per documented sample + seal check, packing and label (team estimate)

science.source: Apollo 15 station 2: ~51 min; no coring or drilling

habitat_egress.source: EMU timeline (15 min egress); confirm with Marco that it is in suit.json

habitat_ingress.source: EMU timeline (15 min ingress); confirm with Marco that it is in suit.json

cache_refill.source: Concept: top-off of suit O2 through the Service and Cooling Umbilical (SCU) mated to the suit DCU (NASA JSC CTSD-ADV-959 Rev A, 2017, sec. 3.2.5.5.2). The 10 min duration and the pre-positioned surface cache are MarsWalk assumptions.

work_metabolic_factor.source: Design average (1200 BTU/h). Apollo geology-station rates were about 0.81-0.89 of it, but we have no Mars data, so we use the conservative value

rest_metabolic_factor.source: O2 burned while the suited crew stands or sits still (airlock egress/ingress, cache refill, waiting in a shelter), relative to P_nom = 1200 BTU/h. 0.5 = 600 BTU/h (176 W): the TOP of the 300-600 BTU/h measured for suited test subjects at rest in a seated position (Rhodes, Bue, Meginnis, Hakam & Radford, 'Thermal Performance Testing of EMU and CSAFE Liquid Cooling Garments', AIAA ICES 2013, NTRS 20130011117, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20130011117/downloads/20130011117.pdf). Cross-check: NASA HIDH nominal awake (shirt-sleeve) O2 use for the 82 kg reference astronaut is 0.57 g/min = 0.40 L/min = ~136 W = ~465 BTU/h (Ewert & Downs, 'Developing a Daily Metabolic Rate Profile for Human Exploration Missions', ICES-2021-365, Table 1, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20205010692/downloads/ICES-2021_Metabolic_Paper-Final.pdf; conversion 1.429 g/L and 20.47 kJ/L at RQ 0.86); Shuttle max awake rate 650 BTU/h (same paper). O2 use scales linearly with metabolic rate (ICES-2026-127 slide 6). We take the top of the suited range because standing in a 104 kg suit at 0.38 g costs more than sitting, and underestimating O2 is the unsafe direction.

sunrise_lmst.source: MCD v6.2; Ls=270 deg; habitat: 77.41359752 E, 18.45369687 N; hourly solar zenith crossing 90 deg; linear interpolation; approximate LTST-to-LMST conversion from LMD; flat horizon; decimal Martian hours. https://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/

sunset_lmst.source: MCD v6.2; Ls=270 deg; habitat: 77.41359752 E, 18.45369687 N; hourly solar zenith crossing 90 deg; linear interpolation; approximate LTST-to-LMST conversion from LMD; flat horizon; decimal Martian hours. https://www-mars.lmd.jussieu.fr/mcd_python/

night_buffer_min.source: Team choice: margin to be back in the habitat before sunset

spe_dose_limit_mSv.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. C (2023), requirement [V1 4031] (4.8.3 Radiation Limits - Solar Particle Events): protect crew from the design-reference SPE (sum of the Oct 1989 events) to < 250 mSv effective dose. Used by the tablet as the stay limit at places that are not radiation-protected. https://standards.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/standards/NASA/C//nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-signature.pdf

w_caution.source: Tunable weight (team default); adjusted with the rover validation

w_obstacle_caution.source: Tunable weight (team default); adjusted with the rover validation
